must_know.title: Strings are immutable
must_know.text: String methods return new strings. If you want the change to persist, assign the result back to a variable.

must_know.title: Escape characters and literal quotes
must_know.text: Use the other quote style or escape the inner quote. Keep three patterns in mind: backslash-n makes a newline, backslash-t makes a tab, and escaped quotes let the string stay open.

must_know.title: Length and indexing basics
must_know.text: len(s) counts every character in the string, and indexing starts at 0.

exam_patterns.title: Rebuild strings instead of assigning into them
exam_patterns.text: If an exam asks to change one character, rebuild the string with slicing instead of assigning by index.

exam_patterns.title: Filter characters in a loop
exam_patterns.text: Use a running result string when the question asks you to keep only the characters that pass a test.

useful_backup.title: Repeat text with *
useful_backup.text: The * operator repeats a string, which sometimes appears in short output questions.

useful_backup.title: Uppercase helper loop
useful_backup.text: A tiny helper can make a filtering loop readable when the test itself is part of what the exam is asking about.

useful_backup.title: Escape-sequence quick table
useful_backup.summary: A compact backup table for the escape and quote patterns that still show up in tiny output questions.

content.text: Keep this low on the page, but it is worth having when a syntax fragment has to be read exactly.

must_know.title: find() versus index()
must_know.text: .find() returns -1 when the substring is missing; .index() raises ValueError.

must_know.title: split() and join() round-trip
must_know.text: .split() turns text into a list, and .join() turns a list back into text with a separator.

must_know.title: replace() returns a new string
must_know.text: .replace(old, new, count) creates a new string and can limit how many replacements happen.

exam_patterns.title: Step slicing and reverse order
exam_patterns.text: Use s[::2] for every second character, s[::-1] to reverse, and negative indices to count from the end.

exam_patterns.title: Boolean string predicates
exam_patterns.text: .islower(), .isupper(), and .isdigit() only return True when the string contains matching cased or digit characters.

exam_patterns.title: Trim whitespace and edges
exam_patterns.text: .strip() removes leading and trailing whitespace; lstrip() and rstrip() remove just one side.

useful_backup.title: String module constants
useful_backup.text: The string module provides ready-made constants such as ascii_lowercase and digits.

useful_backup.title: Search with start/stop
useful_backup.text: find() and index() accept optional start and stop positions when a question needs a bounded search.

content.text: These are the highest-payoff methods to recognize instantly.

must_know.title: f-strings for direct interpolation
must_know.text: F-strings embed expressions inside {} and are the cleanest way to build output strings.

must_know.title: .format() still appears in exams
must_know.text: The older .format() style still appears in exam questions and supports the same width and precision ideas.

must_know.title: join() plus a custom tail
must_know.text: Use join() for the repeated separator, then add the final custom wording separately.

exam_patterns.title: Zero padding and decimal precision
exam_patterns.text: Recognize formatting specs like {:03d} for zero padding and {:.1f} for one decimal place.

exam_patterns.title: Debug output with f'{var=}'
exam_patterns.text: f'{var=}' prints both the variable name and the current value, which is easy to miss in answer choices.

exam_patterns.title: Repeated output with *
exam_patterns.text: The * operator repeats strings and can show up in quick output questions.

useful_backup.title: Legacy format width
useful_backup.text: '{:04d}'.format(n) is the non-f-string version of zero padding and is still worth recognizing.

useful_backup.title: Build the middle, then patch the tail
useful_backup.text: When the last item needs special wording, format the repeated middle first and then patch on the ending.
